title: TCS Wins Multi-Million AI Deal to Run ABB's Global Network Operations, Extending 20-Year Partnership
excerpt: India's largest IT services firm will design and operate ABB's worldwide network infrastructure as an AI-driven service under the new multi-year agreement.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • TCS secures a multi-million AI deal with ABB to enhance global network operations.
  • The contract extends a 20-year partnership, shifting TCS to an end-to-end service model.
  • TCS will implement ABB's Future Network Model, centralizing its network infrastructure.
  • TCS reported a $2.6 billion AI revenue run rate, highlighting its tech leadership.

  • TCS has signed a multi-million, multi-year deal with Swiss-Swedish industrial technology giant ABB to transform its global network operations using AI.
  • The contract extends a 20-year partnership and upgrades TCS's role from managing infrastructure to delivering end-to-end network-as-a-service across ABB's worldwide operations.
  • TCS will design and run ABB's Future Network Model programme, replacing fragmented network environments with a centralized, AI-driven architecture.
  • The deal comes weeks after TCS reported a $2.6 billion AI revenue run rate and a $19 billion JFK Airport technology partnership, reinforcing its position as India's top IT services exporter.

A Two-Decade Partnership Deepens

Tata Consultancy Services has secured a multi-million, multi-year contract from ABB, the Swiss-Swedish electrification and automation giant, to overhaul its global network operations with artificial intelligence. The deal, announced on July 13, marks the next phase of a partnership that stretches back two decades.

Under the expanded agreement, TCS will move beyond its previous role of managing ABB's infrastructure and applications. The Indian IT services leader will now deliver end-to-end global network operations through an integrated network-as-a-service model — designing, integrating, and running ABB's entire network ecosystem as a secure, AI-driven service.

Inside ABB's Future Network Model

At the core of the engagement is ABB's Future Network Model programme, an enterprise-wide initiative to consolidate the company's fragmented network environments into a standardized, centrally managed digital infrastructure. TCS will serve as the strategic programme partner, orchestrating ABB's multi-vendor environment to deliver seamless operations worldwide.

The programme will bring together several critical capabilities under a single framework: service integration and management (SIAM), a global network operations center, advanced cybersecurity protections, and modernized LAN, WAN, and software-defined WAN systems. TCS will also provide end-to-end monitoring and orchestration to ensure high-performance connectivity across ABB's global footprint.

"The Future Network Model represents an important milestone in reinforcing the digital foundation of ABB's global operations. Our association with TCS reflects a shared focus on delivery excellence, continuous enhancement, and building capabilities that can support our strategic priorities."

— Alec Joannou, Group CIO, ABB

TCS's Growing AI Ambitions

The ABB contract is the latest in a string of major wins for TCS, which has been aggressively positioning itself as an AI-first technology partner for global enterprises. The company reported an AI revenue run rate of $2.6 billion in its most recent quarterly results, and last month secured the technology partnership for JFK Airport's $19 billion New Terminal One project.

Transforming ABB's Network Operations
›TCS to deliver end-to-end network operations.
›Implementation of ABB's Future Network Model.
›Focus on service integration and management (SIAM).
›Advanced cybersecurity protections included.

Earlier in the partnership, TCS had consolidated multiple enterprise resource planning systems into a single SAP platform for ABB and led cloud migration projects. The progression from ERP consolidation to AI-driven network operations reflects a broader shift in the Indian IT services industry, where companies like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro are racing to move up the value chain from traditional outsourcing to strategic technology transformation.

What It Means for India's IT Sector

For India's technology workforce, deals of this scale underscore the country's continued dominance in global IT services. TCS employs over 600,000 people, the majority in India, and contract wins like the ABB engagement create downstream demand for AI, cybersecurity, and network engineering talent.

Countries ABB Operates In

ABB operates across electrification, robotics, and automation in more than 100 countries, making network resilience and central oversight critical to its daily operations. The decision to entrust that infrastructure to an Indian firm speaks to the depth of capability that companies like TCS have built over two decades of enterprise technology partnerships.

TCS did not disclose the financial details or precise duration of the contract, according to Reuters.
